a: A press on the curve of an ordered layer inserts an anchor outside its segment's x span, breaking x order
Unmounting the editor mid-drag never reports `onCancel` (nor restores `onInput`) to the dragged layer
A layer whose consumer previews but does not write `onInput` back never commits a drag
A click-empty insert on a `constrain: 'function'` layer can land on an existing anchor's x
The crowding threshold and the drag's spacing read different x spans when `xClamp` is set
Undo/redo compares layer states by identity, so an unchanged layer is reported an edit
Canceling a keyframe key drag leaves the press's selection change in the consumer's state, uncommitted
The rim-contour story's seam drag destroys the other layers' anchors on Escape
b: A press on the curve of an ordered layer can insert an anchor out of x order, and a click commits it that way
A click-empty insert ignores the 'function' constraint's x gap and can put two anchors at one x
The crowding threshold for a press on the curve uses the plot's x span, not the layer's xClamp span that drags use
A click-curve layer with minPoints unset can be deleted below two anchors, after which no press can add one
The keyframe layer's xClamp/yClamp take a reversed pair as a degenerate range; the function layer normalizes it
An arrow key on a bezier handle of a flat keyframe segment rewrites the handle's y, which a drag refuses to do
An edit the consumer declines still records an undo step, so the next Cmd+Z silently does nothing
The rim-contour story's seam move crushes interior anchors onto the seam, breaking its own 'function' constraint
